setting_conditions holds the "Change when running" column as printed: Y = possible, Y* = possible ("the change will immediately take effect; however, the change is not saved into the inverter's memory" until saved with the keypad), N = impossible (page_index 78, printed 5-1).

knowledge_items.title: Application restriction
knowledge_items.description: FRENIC-Mini is designed to drive a three-phase induction motor and three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Fire or an accident could occur otherwise.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not use it for single-phase motors or for other purposes.

knowledge_items.title: Not for life-support systems
knowledge_items.description: Install safety devices for applications where serious accidents or material losses are foreseen in relation to the failure of the inverter.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: FRENIC-Mini may not be used for a life-support system or other purposes directly related to the human safety.

knowledge_items.title: Install on nonflammable material
knowledge_items.description: Otherwise fire could occur. Do not place flammable matter nearby.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Install the inverter on a nonflammable material such as metal.

knowledge_items.title: Do not support by terminal block cover
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause a drop of the inverter and injuries.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not support the inverter by its terminal block cover during transportation.

knowledge_items.title: Keep foreign materials out
knowledge_items.description: Otherwise, a fire or an accident might result.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Prevent lint, paper fibers, sawdust, dust, metallic chips, or other foreign materials from getting into the inverter or from accumulating on the heat sink.

knowledge_items.title: Do not install damaged inverter
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause fire, an accident or injuries.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not install or operate an inverter that is damaged or lacking parts.

knowledge_items.title: Install MCCB/RCD and use specified wire size
knowledge_items.description: Insert a recommended MCCB or RCD/ELCB (with overcurrent protection) in the power line, use devices within the recommended current range and use wires in the specified size. Otherwise fire could occur.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: When wiring the inverter to the power source, insert a recommended molded case circuit breaker (MCCB)

knowledge_items.title: DC reactor required for 500 kVA or more supply
knowledge_items.description: Otherwise, fire could occur.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: When wiring the inverter to the power supply of 500 kVA or more, be sure to connect an optional DC reactor (DCR).

knowledge_items.title: No multicore cable / no surge killer on output
knowledge_items.description: Do not use one multicore cable to connect several inverters with motors. Doing so could cause fire.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not connect a surge killer to the inverter's output (secondary) circuit.

knowledge_items.title: Ground the inverter
knowledge_items.description: Otherwise, electric shock or fire could occur. Ground in compliance with national or local electric code; qualified electricians should wire after turning power off and after installing the inverter body.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Be sure to connect the grounding wires without fail.

knowledge_items.title: Match phases and voltage to supply
knowledge_items.description: Otherwise fire or an accident could occur.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Ensure that the number of input phases and the rated voltage of the product match the number of phases and the voltage of the AC power supply

knowledge_items.title: Do not connect power to output terminals U, V, W
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause fire or an accident.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not connect the power source wires to output terminals (U, V, and W).

knowledge_items.title: Braking resistor connection prohibition
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause fire or an accident.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not insert a braking resistor between terminals P (+) and N (-), P1 and N (-), P (+) and P1, DB and N (-), or P1 and DB.

knowledge_items.title: Control signal wires lack reinforced insulation
knowledge_items.description: If they accidentally touch live parts of the main circuit an extremely high voltage may be applied to the signal lines; protect them from contact with high-voltage lines. Could cause an accident or electric shock.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Generally, control signal wires are not reinforced insulation.

knowledge_items.title: Electric noise
knowledge_items.description: Take care of malfunction of nearby sensors and devices; implement noise control measures.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: The inverter, motor and wiring generate electric noise.

knowledge_items.title: Install terminal block cover before power-on
knowledge_items.description: Otherwise electric shock could occur. Do not operate switches with wet hands.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Be sure to install the terminal block cover before turning the power on. Do not remove the cover while power is applied.

knowledge_items.title: Retry function may restart motor automatically
knowledge_items.description: Design the machinery or equipment so that human safety is ensured after restarting.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: If the retry function has been selected, the inverter may automatically restart and drive the motor depending on the cause of tripping.

knowledge_items.title: Current limiter / automatic deceleration / overload prevention change times
knowledge_items.description: If the stall prevention function (current limiter), automatic deceleration, and overload prevention control have been selected, design the machine so that safety is ensured.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: the inverter may operate at an accelera- tion/deceleration time or frequency different from the set ones.

knowledge_items.title: STOP key and emergency stop
knowledge_items.description: The STOP key is only effective when function setting (F02) has been established to enable the STOP key. If the STOP key priority function is disabled and operation by external commands is enabled, you cannot emergency-stop the inverter using the STOP key on the built-in keypad.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Prepare an emergency stop switch separately.

knowledge_items.title: Alarm reset with run signal ON causes sudden start
knowledge_items.description: Ensure that the operation signal is turned off in advance. Otherwise an accident could occur.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: If an alarm reset is made with the operation signal turned on, a sudden start will occur.

knowledge_items.title: Auto restart after momentary power failure
knowledge_items.description: If F14 = 4 or 5 is enabled, design the machinery or equipment so that human safety is ensured after restarting.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: then the inverter automatically restarts running the motor when the power is recovered.

knowledge_items.title: Wrong function code settings
knowledge_items.description: If you set the function codes wrongly or without completely understanding this manual and the FRENIC-Mini User's Manual an accident or injuries could occur.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: the motor may rotate with a torque or at a speed not permitted for the machine.

knowledge_items.title: Do not touch terminals while powered
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause electric shock.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not touch the inverter terminals while the power is applied to the inverter even if the inverter stops.

knowledge_items.title: Do not switch main power to start/stop
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause failure.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not turn the main circuit power on or off in order to start or stop inverter operation.

knowledge_items.title: Hot heat sink and braking resistor
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause burns.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Do not touch the heat sink or braking resistor because they become very hot.

knowledge_items.title: Brake function is not a mechanical hold
knowledge_items.description: Injuries could occur.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: The brake function of the inverter does not provide mechanical holding means.

knowledge_items.title: Wait before maintenance/inspection
knowledge_items.description: Check that the LED monitor is unlit and the DC link bus voltage between P (+) and N (-) is lower than 25 VDC. Otherwise electric shock could occur. Maintenance only by qualified persons; remove watch and rings; use insulated tools.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Turn the power off and wait for at least five minutes before starting inspection.

knowledge_items.title: Never modify the inverter / disposal
knowledge_items.description: Doing so could cause electric shock or injuries. Handle the inverter as an industrial waste when disposing of it.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Never attempt to modify the inverter.

knowledge_items.title: Reset alarm only with run commands OFF
knowledge_items.description: Remove the cause, check all run commands are OFF, then reset the alarm. Injury may occur.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: If the alarm is released while any run command is set to ON, the inverter may supply the power to the motor, running the motor.

knowledge_items.title: Output voltage can remain after protective function trip
knowledge_items.description: Even though the inverter has interrupted power to the motor, if voltage is applied to the main circuit power input terminals voltage may be output to U, V, W. Turn OFF the power, wait at least five minutes, and confirm DC link bus voltage is +25 VDC or below.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: voltage may be output to inverter output terminals U, V, and W.

knowledge_items.title: EU Low Voltage Directive: RCD/ELCB type
knowledge_items.description: For single-phase 200 V power supplies use type A. Do not use only an RCD/ELCB as the sole electric-shock protection; ground wire size must be greater than power supply lines.
knowledge_items.section: Conformity to the Low Voltage Directive in the EU
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: be sure to install type B of RCD/ELCB on the input (primary) of the inverter if the power source is three-phase 200/400 V.

knowledge_items.title: EU LVD: pollution degree, enclosure, altitude
knowledge_items.description: For Pollution Degree 3 or 4 install in an IP54 or higher enclosure. Enclosure minimum IP2X (top surface IP4X if easily accessible). Above 2000 m basic insulation applies to control circuitry; above 3000 m inverters cannot be used.
knowledge_items.section: Conformity to the Low Voltage Directive in the EU
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: The inverter should be used in an environment that does not exceed Pollution Degree 2 requirements.

knowledge_items.title: EU LVD: mains neutral earthed for 400 V
knowledge_items.description: Short-circuit current test condition: 10 kA supply, max 240 V / max 480 V. Use wires listed in IEC60364-5-52.
knowledge_items.section: Conformity to the Low Voltage Directive in the EU
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: The power supply mains neutral has to be earthed for the three-phase 400 V class inverter.

knowledge_items.title: Instantaneous overcurrent during acceleration
knowledge_items.description: The inverter momentary output current exceeded the overcurrent level (during acceleration).
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Inverter output lines short-circuited. (2) Ground fault at the inverter output lines. (3) Load too heavy / sudden load changes. (4) Excessive torque boost (F37, A13 = 0, 1, 3 or 4). (5) Acceleration/deceleration time too short. (6) Malfunction caused by noise.
knowledge_items.remedy: Remove short-circuited or grounded parts (wires, relay terminals, motor); reduce load or raise inverter capacity; enable instantaneous overcurrent limiting (H12 = 1); decrease torque boost (F09, A05); increase ACC/DEC time (F07, F08, E10, E11), enable current limiter (F43); implement noise measures and enable auto-reset (H04).

knowledge_items.title: Overvoltage during acceleration
knowledge_items.description: The DC link bus voltage was over the detection level of overvoltage.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Power supply voltage exceeded the inverter specification range. (2) Surge current entered the input power supply (phase-advancing capacitor ON/OFF or thyristor converter). (3) Deceleration time too short for load inertia. (4) Acceleration time too short. (5) Braking load too heavy. (6) Malfunction caused by noise.

knowledge_items.title: Undervoltage
knowledge_items.description: DC link bus voltage has dropped below the undervoltage detection level.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Momentary power failure. (2) Power switched back ON too soon (F14 = 1). (3) Supply voltage below inverter specification range. (4) Peripheral equipment malfunction or incorrect connection. (5) Other load caused large starting current / voltage drop. (6) Inrush current caused voltage drop because transformer capacity was insufficient.
knowledge_items.remedy: Reset the alarm; set F14 to 4 or 5 to restart without an alarm; switch power ON again after all keypad LEDs go off; raise voltage to specified range; replace faulty peripherals or correct connections; reconsider power system configuration or transformer capacity.

knowledge_items.title: Input phase loss
knowledge_items.description: Input phase loss occurred, or interphase voltage unbalance rate was large.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Main circuit power input wire broken. (2) Loose input terminal screws. (3) Large interphase voltage unbalance. (4) Cyclic overload. (5) Single-phase voltage input to a three-phase input inverter.
knowledge_items.remedy: Repair/replace input wires; tighten terminal screws to the recommended torque; connect an AC reactor (ACR) or raise inverter capacity; apply three-phase power. The input phase loss protection can be disabled with H98.

knowledge_items.title: Output phase loss
knowledge_items.description: Output phase loss occurred.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Inverter output wires broken. (2) Motor winding broken. (3) Loose output terminal screws. (4) Single-phase motor connected.
knowledge_items.remedy: Replace output wires or motor; tighten terminal screws to the recommended torque; single-phase motors cannot be used (FRENIC-Mini only drives three-phase induction motors).
knowledge_items.section: 6.3 If an Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Problem Output phase loss occurred.

knowledge_items.title: Heat sink overheat
knowledge_items.description: Temperature around the heat sink has risen abnormally.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Ambient temperature exceeded specification. (2) Ventilation path blocked. (3) Cooling fan life expired or fan faulty. (4) Load too heavy.
knowledge_items.remedy: Lower the ambient temperature, ensure clearance; clean the heat sink; replace the cooling fan; reduce load (use overload early warning E34), decrease carrier frequency (F26), enable overload prevention control (H70).
knowledge_items.section: 6.3 If an Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor

knowledge_items.title: External alarm
knowledge_items.description: External alarm was inputted (THR assigned to a digital input terminal).
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Alarm function of external equipment activated. (2) Wrong connection or poor contact in external alarm signal wiring. (3) Incorrect function code data (THR assignment or normal/negative logic mismatch).
knowledge_items.remedy: Remove the cause of the external alarm; connect the signal wire correctly (E01 to E03, E98, E99 set to 9); match normal/negative logic.
knowledge_items.section: 6.3 If an Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Problem External alarm was inputted ( THR ).

knowledge_items.title: Motor protection (PTC thermistor)
knowledge_items.description: Temperature of the motor has risen abnormally.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Motor ambient temperature exceeded range. (2) Motor cooling system defective. (3) Load too heavy. (4) PTC activation level (H27) set inadequately. (5) Improper PTC/pull-up resistor connections or values. (6) Excessive torque boost. (7) V/f pattern mismatch. (8) Thermistor mode enabled (H26) though no PTC is used.
knowledge_items.remedy: Lower temperature, repair cooling, reduce load, increase carrier frequency (F26); modify H27; correct connections and resistor; decrease torque boost; match F04/F05 (A02/A03) to nameplate; set H26 = 0.
knowledge_items.section: 6.3 If an Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Problem Temperature of the motor has risen abnormally.

knowledge_items.title: Braking resistor overheated
knowledge_items.description: The electronic thermal protection for the braking resistor has been activated. The inverter monitors the magnitude of the braking load, not the resistor surface temperature.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Braking load too heavy. (2) Deceleration time too short. (3) Incorrect F50 and F51 data.
knowledge_items.remedy: Lower the braking load; increase deceleration time (F08, E11); review braking resistor performance and reconfigure F50 and F51.
knowledge_items.section: 6.3 If an Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Problem The electronic thermal protection for the braking resistor has been activated.

knowledge_items.title: Motor 1 overload
knowledge_items.description: Electronic thermal protection for motor 1 activated.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Electronic thermal characteristics do not match motor overload characteristics. (2) Activation level inadequate. (3) ACC/DEC time too short. (4) Load too heavy.
knowledge_items.remedy: Reconsider P99, F10, F12; use an external thermal relay; change F11; increase ACC/DEC time; reduce load.

knowledge_items.title: Inverter overload
knowledge_items.description: Temperature inside inverter has risen abnormally.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Ambient temperature exceeded range. (2) Excessive torque boost. (3) ACC/DEC time too short. (4) Load too heavy. (5) Ventilation paths blocked. (6) Cooling fan life expired or faulty. (7) Long motor wires causing large leakage current.
knowledge_items.remedy: Lower the temperature; decrease torque boost; increase ACC/DEC time; reduce load, decrease F26, enable H70; ensure clearance, clean heat sink, replace fan; insert an output circuit filter (OFL).

knowledge_items.cause: (1) Inverter shut down during writing of function code data (initialization or copying). (2) Strong electrical noise when writing data. (3) Control circuit error.
knowledge_items.remedy: Initialize with H03 = 1 and check if the reset key resets the alarm; revert data to previous settings; implement noise measures; if defective the control PCB must be replaced - contact Fuji Electric representative.

knowledge_items.remedy: Re-insert the connector, replace cable; implement noise measures; replace the keypad.

knowledge_items.title: Tuning error
knowledge_items.description: Auto-tuning failed.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Phase missing between inverter and motor. (2) V/f or motor rated current not properly set. (3) Wiring length exceeds 50 m. (4) Motor capacity three or more ranks lower or two or more ranks higher than inverter. (5) Special motor such as high-speed motor. (6) Rotating tuning (P04 or A18 = 2) attempted while brake applied.
knowledge_items.remedy: Connect motor properly; check F04, F05, H50 to H53, P02, P03 (motor 2: A02, A03, A16, A17); shorten wiring; replace inverter with appropriate capacity or set P06, P07, P08 (A20, A21, A22) manually; disable auto-tuning and auto-torque boost (F37 or A13 = 1); use P04 or A18 = 1 or release the brake.

knowledge_items.title: RS-485 communications error
knowledge_items.description: A communications error occurred during RS-485 communication.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Inverter communications conditions (y01 to y10) do not match the host equipment. (2) No communication within the cycle although no-response error detection time (y08) is set. (3) Host equipment (PLC, computer) not operating due to incorrect settings or defect. (4) RS-485 converter not operating (connection, settings, hardware). (5) Broken cable or poor contact. (6) Strong electrical noise.
knowledge_items.remedy: Correct the y code mismatch; change host software or disable no-response detection (y08 = 0); remove cause of host/converter error; replace cable; implement noise measures and replace the RS-485 converter with a recommended insulated one.

knowledge_items.remedy: Remove the cause of rapid discharge; after resetting the alarm, revert the relevant function code data to original values; implement noise measures; if erf occurs each time power is switched ON the control PCB is defective - contact Fuji Electric representative.

knowledge_items.title: Step-out detection (PMSM)
knowledge_items.description: The step-out of the PMSM was detected.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Mismatch with motor characteristics. (2) Insufficient starting torque. (3) Light load. (4) Control system not stabilized.
knowledge_items.remedy: Set motor parameters F04, F05, P02, P03, P60 to P63; adjust acceleration time (F07, E10), raise P74, set F24, S-curve (H07 = 1 or 2), raise P89; lower P74 for light load (80% or lower when running motor alone); adjust P60, P91, P92.

knowledge_items.title: Motor does not rotate
knowledge_items.description: The motor does not rotate.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) No power supplied to the inverter. (2) No run forward/reverse command input or both input (external operation). (3) No rotation direction indicated (keypad operation). (4) Inverter in Programming mode. (5) Higher-priority run command active. (6) Reference frequency below starting/stop frequency. (7) Higher-priority frequency command active. (8) Frequency limiters F15/F16 wrong. (9) Coast-to-stop command effective. (10) Broken wire or poor contact to motor. (11) Overload. (12) Insufficient motor torque. (13) Wrong connection or poor contact of DC reactor.
knowledge_items.remedy: Turn ON MCCB/RCD/MC and check voltage; input run command, correct E98/E99 and terminal wiring, check sink/source jumper; set F02 = 0, 2 or 3; switch to Running mode; correct H30; set frequency above F23/F25; correct F15/F16; release BX; repair motor wiring, release brake, increase torque boost (F09, A05), match V/f pattern; correct DCR wiring.
knowledge_items.section: 6.2 If No Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: [ 1 ] The motor does not rotate.

knowledge_items.title: Motor rotates but speed does not increase
knowledge_items.description: The motor rotates, but the speed does not increase.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Maximum frequency F03/A01 too low. (2) Frequency limiter F15 too low. (3) Reference frequency too low. (4) Higher-priority frequency command (multistep, link) active with low reference. (5) ACC time too long/short. (6) Overload / mechanical brake. (7) Mismatch with motor characteristics; current limiter F43/F44 active. (8) Current limiting prevented frequency increase. (9) Bias and gain incorrectly set.
knowledge_items.remedy: Correct F03/A01, F15; increase reference frequency; correct function codes; change F07/E10; reduce load; perform auto-tuning; correct F44 or set F43 = 0; adjust torque boost F09; match V/f pattern (F04, F05, H50 to H53); readjust F18, C50, C32, C34, C37, C39.
knowledge_items.section: 6.2 If No Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: [ 2 ] The motor rotates, but the speed does not increase.

knowledge_items.title: Motor runs in the opposite direction
knowledge_items.description: The motor runs in the opposite direction to the command.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Wiring to the motor incorrect. (2) Incorrect connection/settings of FWD/REV (E98, E99). (3) Keypad run command with wrong rotation direction setting (F02).
knowledge_items.remedy: Connect U, V, W of inverter to U, V, W of motor; correct E98/E99 and terminals; change F02 to 2 or 3.
knowledge_items.section: 6.2 If No Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: [ 3 ] The motor runs in the opposite direction to the command.

knowledge_items.title: Speed fluctuation or current oscillation (hunting)
knowledge_items.description: Speed fluctuation or current oscillation occurs during running at constant speed.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Frequency command fluctuates. (2) External potentiometer affected by noise. (3) Frequency switching or multistep relay chattering. (4) Long wiring between inverter and motor / auto controls. (5) Load rigidity low or special motor parameters.
knowledge_items.remedy: Increase filter constants (C33, C38); isolate/shield control wires; connect a capacitor or ferrite core; replace relay; perform auto-tuning, select constant torque load (F37, A13 = 1), shorten output wires, readjust H80/A41; decrease F26 or set F27 = 0.
knowledge_items.section: 6.2 If No Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: [ 4 ] Speed fluctuation or current oscillation (e.g., hunting) occurs during running at constant speed.

knowledge_items.title: Grating sound or fluctuating motor sound
knowledge_items.description: Grating sound is heard from the motor or the motor sound fluctuates.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) Carrier frequency too low. (2) Ambient temperature too high with automatic carrier lowering enabled (H98). (3) Resonance with the load.
knowledge_items.remedy: Increase F26, change F27; lower the panel temperature (over 40 degC) or reduce load; adjust jump frequencies C01 to C04 to avoid resonance. Note: if H98 is disabled an 0h1 or 0lu alarm may occur.
knowledge_items.section: 6.2 If No Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: [ 5 ] Grating sound is heard from the motor or the motor sound fluctuates.

knowledge_items.title: Motor does not accelerate/decelerate in specified time
knowledge_items.description: The motor does not accelerate or decelerate within the specified time.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) S-curve or curvilinear pattern (H07). (2) Current limiting prevented frequency increase. (3) Automatic deceleration (H69) active. (4) Overload. (5) Insufficient torque. (6) Noise on external potentiometer. (7) Wrong ACC/DEC time selection (RT1).
knowledge_items.remedy: Select linear pattern H07 = 0 and shorten times; adjust F44 or disable F43; increase deceleration time; reduce load; increase torque boost; isolate wiring/add capacitor or ferrite core; correct RT1 setting.
knowledge_items.section: 6.2 If No Alarm Code Appears on the LED Monitor
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: [ 6 ] The motor does not accelerate or decelerate within the specified time.

knowledge_items.title: Motor does not restart after momentary power failure
knowledge_items.description: The motor does not restart even after the power recovers from a momentary power failure.
knowledge_items.cause: (1) F14 is 0 or 1. (2) Run command remains OFF after power restored (3-wire HLD or control power shut down).
knowledge_items.remedy: Change F14 to 4 or 5; check power recovery sequence; allow a run command to be issued again within 2 seconds after power is restored.
